title: Centered chi-squared MGF bound
statement:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $k$ be a positive natural number. Suppose $Y:\Omega\to\bbr$ is measurable and normally distributed with mean $0$ and variance $1/k$, that is, its law $Y_*\mu$ equals $N(0,1/k)$. Then for every real $t$ with $\abs{t}\le k/4$, the function $\omega\mapsto \exp\!\bigl(t\,(Y(\omega)^2 - 1/k)\bigr)$ is $\mu$-integrable, and the moment generating function of the centered variable $Y^2 - 1/k$ satisfies
\[
  \E_\mu\!\left[e^{t(Y^2 - 1/k)}\right] \;\le\; \exp\!\Bigl(\frac{2t^2}{k^2}\Bigr).
\]
hypotheses_covered: $k$ is a positive natural number ($0 < k$)
replaced:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, $k>0$, and let $Y:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$
be measurable with $Y_*\mu = N(0,1/k)$.  For every $t\in\mathbb{R}$ with
$|t|\le k/4$, the map $\omega\mapsto\exp\bigl(t(Y(\omega)^2-1/k)\bigr)$ is
$\mu$-integrable and
\[
  \mathbb{E}_\mu\!\left[e^{t(Y^2 - 1/k)}\right]
  \;\le\; \exp\!\Bigl(\frac{2t^2}{k^2}\Bigr).
\]
